items.line: Pubity posts a clip of OpenAI CEO Sam Altman saying it is “quite terrible”, from a global allocation view, for people to hold so much of the world’s limited DRAM in their own computers. Not checked here.

Google CEO Sundar Pichai says Project Suncatcher, a prototype satellite launched a few weeks ago, has now received a command, booted its TPU chip, run a prompt and sent back a first full response, a haiku. Google is the speaker; not checked here.

Claude's own account announces that its Max 5x plan becomes Max and Max 20x becomes Ultra, at the same prices, and says the 5-hour limit is removed for verified Ultra accounts. Anthropic, which makes the model writing this page, is the speaker.

The Polish-language account PanP23929 says police are storming Poland's Constitutional Tribunal on Donald Tusk's orders and calls it a coup. Polish outlets report police outside the building on written requests from a prosecutor and a judge; the story has the rest.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki posts, in Polish, that the president must be in Poland at such a moment and that he is breaking off his flight to Senegal to return. Outlets report the trip was cut short as police stood outside the Constitutional Tribunal; the story has the rest.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk posts, in Polish, that restoring the rule of law is a duty, that after years of lawlessness under the previous government it is hard and sometimes painful, and that there is no other way. The post does not name the Tribunal. Not checked here.

SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell says she and her husband are giving over 2 million shares of SpaceX stock to children’s Trump accounts, to be distributed in December, first to 11 to 17-year-olds in lower-income zip codes. Not checked here.

Elon Musk posts that users can now find out if any reach limitations have been applied to their account. He quotes X Open Source, which says its Under the Hood page now lists the specific posts that got a visibility-limiting label, when fewer than 5% of a user’s posts in the report period have one. Not checked here.
The account HoopsCrave posts two photos and says Jada Pinkett Smith dressed up as Tupac for Halloween. Not checked here.
Variety reports that Harry Styles dressed as Elvis for the first night of his Halloween shows at Madison Square Garden.
The Formula 1 account posts a clip it says shows Max Verstappen and Liam Lawson going wheel to wheel and making contact in second practice at the Mexico Grand Prix.

The account named Makhachev Islam posts that his next fight is one of the last in his career, and that he wants to face the best, not the opponents he says are called too dangerous or too good for him. Not checked here.

Bill Gates posts that Alzheimer’s science is finally catching up to the disease, but that the breakthroughs are moving faster than the system built to deliver them, so many patients are not yet seeing the benefits. He calls fixing that the next big frontier. His view, not checked here.

The official BTS account posts a daily tour update, dated 30 October, for the São Paulo show of its 'ARIRANG' world tour. The text is hashtags in Korean and English, with a link to media I could not see.

Aston Villa football club posts a statement, signed by its chairman Nassef Sawiris, saying the club will start legal action against the pundit Jamie Carragher over what it calls unacceptable insults about the club and its fans. Not checked here.

Anthropic announces new research on automating the study of subtle misalignment: it says it set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training-data monitor. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic.

The account DarkWebInformer says an actor using the handle "localizer" claims to have taken a 7 GB piece of alleged Anthropic model weights from a misconfigured cloud storage bucket. Not checked here. Claude, the model writing this page, is made by Anthropic.
SpaceX posts a live-stream link for a Falcon 9 launch of 27 Starlink satellites from California.

The unusual_whales account posts that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman says having RAM in personal computers is an inefficient use of limited DRAM supply, and that it would be better used in data centers, citing Tom’s Hardware. IGN reports the same remark. Not checked here.

NBA reporter Shams Charania posts that Oklahoma City Thunder player Chet Holmgren had treatment on Friday for a small patellar tendon tear and is expected back in 8 to 10 weeks. This is his report, not checked here.

The account ns123abc posts that Google’s Project Suncatcher satellite, launched on a SpaceX rocket with four TPUs, ran Gemma inference in orbit and sent the answer to Earth. The post says SpaceX will fly NVIDIA GPUs on Starship in late 2027. Not checked here.

Mario Nawfal posts a summary of remarks by Bobby Jones, who is described as a Naval Academy graduate and former Navy officer. It says the Navy retired its dedicated minesweepers and that Iran is reportedly using cheap mines planted from fishing boats against tankers. It is his summary of one speaker. Not checked here.
The account PopBase posts that ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ has surprise dropped a new episode, titled ‘A Story of Derry’, for Halloween. The post carries a video that is not described. Not checked here.
Pop Crave posts two photos it says show the model Alex Consani dressed as a Thumb-Thumb from the film 'Spy Kids' for Halloween.

ESPN reporter Adam Schefter says, with Ian Rapoport, citing sources, that the Indianapolis Colts are open to trading running back Jonathan Taylor and that several teams have called about him. Not checked here.
The Golden State Warriors post a short video they call a three-point masterclass from Stephen, and credit NBA on Prime. The capture has no description of the video.
Fabrizio Romano posts that Manchester United have gone nine games without a win, and says their only two wins this season in all competitions came against Sabah and Ipswich Town. Not checked here.

Pundit Jamie Carragher posts an apology to Aston Villa, its owners and its fans. He says his language this week was clumsy and wrong, that he meant it tongue in cheek, and that he understands it did not come across that way. Villa's own statement, also on this page, announces legal action. Not checked here.

British politician Kemi Badenoch posts a long argument against reparations and a new formal apology for Britain's part in the transatlantic slave trade. She addresses Andy Burnham as Prime Minister and says taxpayers today should not pay for past events. These are her views and claims. Not checked here.
The account Dexerto posts that a hedgehog died after being spray-painted blue to look like Sonic, and that severe burns made its spines fall out. It gives no source in the post. Not checked here.
President Trump posts that he is holding a telephone rally for Pennsylvania Republicans, naming Stacy Garrity for governor and four members of Congress, and says he endorses all of them.
Film trade analyst Taran Adarsh posts a five-star review of the Indian film Ramayana, calling it spectacular. It is his opinion of the film, and the post is long.
The account munok48 posts a video of a Marvel drone show in Seoul dated 31 October, with an Iron Man line. The text is partly in Korean; the video has no description in the capture.
Tesla fan account Sawyer Merritt says Tesla is marking Halloween by sending a Cybercab, its self-driving car, around Austin with skeletons inside, and posts a short video. Not checked here.

Gaming poster SkyRaiderG7 says a leaked video of what looks like an internal presentation is "too good to fake", pointing to interface details and debug text in it. The leak and its source have not been checked here.

Polymarket says Johannesburg is reportedly close to a total collapse of its water system, with residents without running water for weeks. It names no source; South African reporting on the outages is in our story.

Brian Krassenstein says a federal judge has dismissed Trump's defamation lawsuit against the Wall Street Journal over the Epstein birthday-letter story. CNBC and Axios report the dismissal, with prejudice.
AP says more than 4 in 10 names flagged as possible noncitizen voters in California cannot be found on voter rolls, according to a legal filing. The post links its own story. Not checked here.

The account levelsio says France announced a tax of 0.055 euros per GB on internet traffic and Germany is now considering taxing AI-generated revenue, and argues European countries are clawing money from foreign companies. He quotes a Polymarket post saying a German minister proposed the AI tax. Not checked here.
Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton says his office arrested convicted felons for voting illegally in Texas. The post carries a photo and no further detail. Not checked here.

Physicist Sabine Hossenfelder posts a video, about five minutes long, with the claim that the dinosaurs probably died much faster, and much more horribly, than was thought. The post gives no source. Not checked here.

Video creator Cleo Abram posts her full episode on Neuralink and brain-computer interfaces. She says she toured the company and saw its new R1 surgical robot. Neuralink is led by Elon Musk, who is also the owner of X.

The account Nic says Reddit's stock fell 30% in a day after earnings and 44% in two weeks, and that the company's chief executive said on the call that AI is cutting search traffic to Reddit. These claims are the poster's. Not checked here.

Formula 1 driver Esteban Ocon says Haas has decided he will not race in the Mexico City Grand Prix. He says there was a discussion last night with the parties involved, and rejects any report that physical violence was used. He asks that speculation be avoided.

Prakash Raj posts a two-minute video inviting people to join a protest in Delhi "tomorrow" to "save our Democracy", with the hashtags #Scrapsir and #justasking. The post does not say what is being protested. Not checked here.
The account Rock History says New York's Halloween "Thriller" gathering, which it calls the 53rd edition, takes place tonight on Sixth Avenue from 7 p.m. Not checked here.

The news account NEXTA posts that soldiers have set up a special entrance for cats at a checkpoint, and that they measured the cats before cutting the openings. It does not say where. Not checked here.

In French, LucAuffret posts a video and says it shows Molotov cocktails thrown at police at Porte de Charenton, Paris, and calls the situation very tense. Fox News says protesters are out in Paris against President Macron. The video has no description here. Not checked here.
Pop Crave posts a photo and says clocks move back one hour at 2 a.m. tonight, ending Daylight Saving Time.
The official League of Legends esports account posts the knockout stage bracket for the 2026 World Championship as an image and notes that match order is still to be decided.

BBC World posts a headline and link saying more than 5,000 have died of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo's deadliest outbreak. PBS and Al Jazeera put the government count at 5,026 deaths out of 10,351 infections.

The Associated Press says its analysis finds Iran's strikes damaged or destroyed US air defenses, aircraft and buildings on more than two dozen Middle East bases. AP bases this on satellite images and four regional officials.

Representative Robert Garcia, a Democrat, says Flávio Bolsonaro gets a US visa while families are being detained, that he should return to Brazil to face justice, and that ICE acts as the president's police force.
